title: contrast
universal_lens: The WCAG contrast audit formalizes a perceptual metric space. By mapping chromatic coordinates to relative luminance, we define a distance operator. The threshold acts as a discontinuous step function, enforcing a minimum geodesic separation between foreground signal and background noise in the visual manifold.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, contrast ratios serve as a proxy for feature separability within high-dimensional telemetry. A sub-threshold ratio represents an epistemic blind spot where Bayesian posterior updates fail to diverge from priors. We apply conformal inference to bound the uncertainty of low-contrast data points.
gse_mapping: For GSE, the cockpit's dark theme is a dynamic state-space. Low-contrast elements represent degenerate transitions where situational awareness collapses. Correcting colors to hit AA compliance acts as a control-theoretic feedback loop, ensuring robust state observation and preventing catastrophic decision-making failures.

primitives.name: Luminance Contrast Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: For every text-on-background pair, compute the contrast ratio and flag anything below 4.5:1 (3:1 for text ≥24px or bold ≥19px).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: C: dimensionless contrast ratio; L_f: relative foreground luminance [0,1]; L_b: relative background luminance [0,1].
primitives.assumptions: Perceptual uniformity of luminance scaling; sRGB color space linearity after gamma correction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when L_f = L_b, yielding C=1, resulting in total information loss and zero discriminability.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the Mahalanobis distance in GSI feature spaces, measuring the statistical separation between a signal vector and its baseline noise covariance.
layer2.telemetry: Computed WCAG contrast ratio across all UI DOM nodes.

primitives.name: Chromatic Manifold Projection
primitives.verbatim_quote: Prioritize low-contrast gray-on-dark body text (the Recommended next actions list in `apps/web/app/cockpit/page.tsx`, stat sub-labels, decision-queue body) and colored text on dark (crimson warnings, gold/cyan labels).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: H, S, V: Hue, Saturation, Value components; V maps to relative luminance [0,1].
primitives.assumptions: Human visual system sensitivity is predominantly driven by luminance rather than chrominance in low-light (dark theme) regimes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Achromatic collapse: highly saturated colors (crimson, cyan) projecting onto identical low-luminance values against a near-black background.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE hazard detection kernels, where distinct threat vectors (colored labels) must maintain orthogonal projection distances to prevent cognitive aliasing.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency distribution of chroma-to-luma ratios in active warning states.

primitives.name: Compliance Correction Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: For each fail, give the current ratio and a corrected color that hits AA while staying on-palette.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: ΔE: CIEDE2000 color difference metric [dimensionless]; T_AA: Accessibility threshold constant.
primitives.assumptions: The design palette forms a continuous, navigable Riemannian manifold allowing gradient descent toward accessibility constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Palette boundary saturation: the nearest accessible color lies outside the predefined brand gamut, forcing a structural redesign.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI parameter recalibration under strict regulatory bounds, finding the minimal perturbation to model weights that satisfies fairness constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Magnitude of hex-code perturbations required to achieve AA compliance.

reasoning_traces.think:
The provided excerpts outline a rigorous audit of visual perception thresholds within a software cockpit. Mathematically, this translates to defining a metric tensor over the RGB color space, specifically targeting the dark-theme regime. The core operator is the contrast ratio, a non-linear transformation of linearized luminance values. This operator measures the geodesic distance between a foreground signal (text) and background noise (theme). When this distance falls below a critical eigenvalue (4.5:1), the system enters a failure regime characterized by information entropy maximization—the user cannot distinguish the signal.

We derive three sovereign primitives from this process. First, the Luminance Contrast Operator establishes the fundamental measurement kernel. Second, the Chromatic Manifold Projection identifies specific high-risk sub-manifolds (e.g., crimson warnings on dark backgrounds) where high saturation fails to compensate for low luminance, leading to perceptual aliasing. Third, the Compliance Correction Kernel acts as a constrained optimization routine. It seeks the nearest point on the permissible design manifold that satisfies the accessibility inequality. In the context of Galaxy Sports Intelligence, these primitives map directly to feature separability and anomaly detection. If our telemetry data lacks sufficient 'contrast' against the baseline noise, our predictive models suffer from high variance and poor calibration. The audit process is essentially a hyperparameter tuning exercise for human-machine interfaces, ensuring that the informational bandwidth of the cockpit matches the cognitive processing limits of the operator.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive lineage traces back to the Weber-Fechner law in psychophysics, which posits that perceived intensity is logarithmic to physical stimulus. It further connects to Helmholtz's work on visual perception and modern colorimetry standards established by the CIE. The mathematical formalization relies heavily on linear algebra transformations from device-dependent RGB to perceptually uniform spaces like CIELAB, bridging 19th-century sensory theory with 21st-century digital accessibility mandates.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model two opposing agents: the System Architect and the Cognitive Operator. The Architect aims to minimize visual clutter and maximize aesthetic cohesion, often pushing colors toward low-contrast, harmonious palettes. The Operator, however, operates under extreme time pressure and requires maximum signal-to-noise ratio to make split-second decisions. The audit acts as a Nash equilibrium mechanism, forcing the Architect to yield ground on aesthetics to satisfy the Operator's survival-level need for discriminability, preventing catastrophic misinterpretation of critical alerts.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A cross-layer veto is triggered if the corrected colors, while mathematically compliant with WCAG AA, introduce severe chromatic aberration or violate the fundamental brand identity constraints of the platform. Furthermore, if the contrast improvement relies solely on increasing font weight without altering luminance, it may cause layout shifts that break the underlying CSS grid topology. We must also veto any correction that creates a 'halo effect' due to excessive brightness differences, which can induce visual fatigue and degrade long-term situational awareness in the cockpit environment.
